Appendix B • Proofs & Comments

B.11 Flat Torsion-Free Connections (§6.4)

Proposition. A torsion-free connection satisfies \(\mathrm{Riem} = 0\) on an open set \(\mathcal{W}\) if and only if around every \(p \in \mathcal{W}\) there is a chart \((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\) with \(\Gamma_\mathscr{Y} = 0\).

  • (\(\Leftarrow\)) If \(\Gamma_\mathscr{Y} = 0\), the component functions of \(\mathrm{Riem}\) vanish in \((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\) (Chapter 6), so the tensor field \(\mathrm{Riem}\) vanishes on \(\mathcal{V}\).

  • (\(\Rightarrow\)) Parallel covector fields. Take a chart \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\) with \(\mathscr{X}(p) = 0\), a cube \(C = (-r, r)^d \subseteq \mathscr{X}(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{W})\), and write component functions as functions of the coordinates \(\alpha \in C\), with \(\partial_k \coloneqq \partial / \partial \alpha^k\). A covector field \(\mathsf{X} = \mathtt{x}_i \, dx^i\) is parallel, \(\nabla \mathsf{X} = 0\), if \begin{align*} \partial_k \mathtt{x}_i = \Gamma^j_{ik} \, \mathtt{x}_j, \qquad \forall \, i, k. \tag{P} \end{align*} Differentiating (P) and using it again, \(0 = \partial_m \partial_k \mathtt{x}_i - \partial_k \partial_m \mathtt{x}_i = \mathrm{Riem}^j_{imk} \, \mathtt{x}_j\), so flatness is exactly the condition for (P) to be solvable with arbitrary values at \(p\). Explicitly, solve the \(k = 1\) equation along the \(\alpha^1\)-axis, then the \(k = 2\) equation along \(\alpha^2\) from every point reached, and so on up to \(k = d\), each step being a linear system of ordinary differential equations with a unique smooth solution on \((-r, r)\). After step \(s\), the defect \(w_i \coloneqq \partial_k \mathtt{x}_i - \Gamma^j_{ik} \mathtt{x}_j\) of any earlier equation, \(k < s\), satisfies \begin{align*} \partial_s w_i = \Gamma^j_{is} \, w_j - \mathrm{Riem}^j_{isk} \, \mathtt{x}_j = \Gamma^j_{is} \, w_j, \end{align*} with \(w_i = 0\) at \(\alpha^s = 0\), hence \(w_i = 0\): all equations of (P) hold on \(C\).

  • Parallel coframe. Starting from \((d\mathscr{X}^a)_p\), this yields parallel covector fields \(\mathsf{X}^a = \mathtt{x}^a_{i} \, dx^i\), \(a = 1, \dots, d\), with \(\det(\mathtt{x}^a_{i}) = 1\) at \(\alpha = 0\), hence non-zero on \(C\) after shrinking \(r\).

  • Coordinates. Since \(\nabla\) is torsion-free, \(\Gamma^j_{ik} = \Gamma^j_{ki}\), so (P) gives \(\partial_k \mathtt{x}^a_{i} = \partial_i \mathtt{x}^a_{k}\). On \(C\), the functions \begin{align*} F^a(\alpha) \coloneqq \int_0^1 \mathtt{x}^a_{i}(\lambda \alpha) \, \alpha^i \, d\lambda \qquad \text{satisfy} \qquad \partial_k F^a(\alpha) = \int_0^1 \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ \lambda \, \mathtt{x}^a_{k}(\lambda \alpha) \Big] d\lambda = \mathtt{x}^a_{k}(\alpha), \end{align*} where the symmetry was used to recognize the total derivative. The Jacobian of \(F\) is \((\mathtt{x}^a_{k})\), invertible, so by the inverse function theorem \(\mathscr{Y}^a \coloneqq F^a \circ \mathscr{X}\) defines a chart \((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\) around \(p\) in the maximal atlas, with \(d\mathscr{Y}^a = \mathtt{x}^a_{k} \, dx^k = \mathsf{X}^a\).

  • Vanishing coefficients. In \((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\), the parallel covector fields \(dy^a\) have constant component functions \(\delta^a_i\), so \(0 = \big( \nabla_{\partial y_k} dy^a \big)_i = - \left( \Gamma_\mathscr{Y} \right)^a_{ik}\) for all \(a, i, k\). \(\square\)

  • Remarks. Torsion-freeness is necessary: \(\Gamma_\mathscr{Y} = 0\) implies \(\mathtt{T} = 0\), so charts with \(\Gamma = 0\) exist if and only if \(\mathrm{Riem} = 0\) and \(\mathtt{T} = 0\). The result is local: a flat torus, for instance, admits such charts around every point but no global one. Two such charts differ by an affine change of coordinates, since their transition map has vanishing second derivatives by the transformation law.
